synthesis.body: Bash `find . -not -path './node_modules/*' -not -path './.git/*'` is anchored at the leading `./` — only TOP-level `node_modules` or `.git` are excluded. The Python equivalent `if "node_modules" in path.parts` excludes a `node_modules` segment at ANY depth, so a nested `packages/x/node_modules/y/AGENTS.md` is silently skipped where bash would still apply the per-package lint. The divergence is invisible until someone adds a nested vendor dir, at which point lint coverage shrinks without warning. The fix: `if path.parts[:1] in (("node_modules",), (".git",))` — anchor to position 0. Surfaced in the post-EXECUTE adversarial review of windows-hooks-phase3's lint-agents-md.py port. The general rule for path-glob transliteration: read the bash glob as anchored (`./X/*` = top-level) or unanchored (`*/X/*` = any depth) and pick the Python predicate that matches the anchor, not the substring.

title: Bash-to-Python port: `"foo" in path.parts` matches segment at *any* depth where bash `-not -path './foo/*'` was top-level-anchored
